rationale: C24 is the January 12 letter that the child expressly identifies as its own earlier proposal and then answers point by point. The child reuses C24's numbered diplomatic structure, revisits its proposals concerning the United Nations, outer space, nuclear controls, Eastern Europe, and a summit, and repeats distinctive language about a top-level meeting holding good hope of advancing peace and justice. This is direct continuation and reuse of concrete drafting, not merely shared subject matter. C16 and C22 have related disarmament and Soviet-relations language, but neither matches the child's structure and exact responsive relationship nearly as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I tried in my letter to you of January 12 to put forward some new ideas. For example, I proposed strengthening the United Nations by rededication of our nations to its purposes and principles, with the accompaniment of some reduction in the use of the veto power in the Security Council.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I propose, Mr. Chairman, that we should rededicate ourselves to the United Nations, its Principles and Purposes and to our Charter obligations.... I propose that we should make it the policy of our two governments at least not to use veto power to prevent the Security Council from proposing methods for the pacific settlement of disputes
shared_material.explanation: The child explicitly identifies and summarizes C24's concrete United Nations and veto proposal.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Another new idea was that outer space should be perpetually dedicated to peaceful purposes.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I propose that we agree that outer space should be used only for peaceful purposes.... Should not outer space be dedicated to the peaceful uses of mankind and denied to the purposes of war?
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive outer-space proposal and dedication language are carried directly from C24 into the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Perhaps the impasse... can be broken by less formal and less publicized contacts through which we would continue to seek to find out whether there can be a top-level meeting which... “would hold good hope of advancing the cause of peace and justice in the world.”
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It would be essential that prior to such a meeting these complex matters should be worked on in advance through diplomatic channels and by our Foreign Ministers... so that it can be ascertained that such a top-level meeting would, in fact, hold good hope of advancing the cause of peace and justice in the world.
shared_material.explanation: The child quotes C24's distinctive summit criterion verbatim and preserves its machinery of diplomatic and foreign-minister preparation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I noted that Mr. Khrushchev devoted a considerable part of his Minsk speech to a discussion of conditions in Hungary, Poland, and East Germany.... why cannot we both discuss them?
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The second situation to which I refer is that of the countries of Eastern Europe.... I propose that we should now discuss this matter.
shared_material.explanation: The child continues and defends C24's proposal for bilateral discussion of Eastern European conditions.
